q: (Only Allaah knows the correct meaning of these letters.)
v.s: Tā, Seen, Meem.
v.c: Ṭâ-Sĩn-Mĩm.

v.s: These are the verses of the clear Book.
v.c: These are the verses of the clear Book.

q: It seems like you will destroy yourself
v.s: Perhaps, [O Muhammad], you would kill yourself with grief that they will not be believers.
v.c: Perhaps you ˹O Prophet˺ will grieve yourself to death over their disbelief.

q: If We willed, We could have revealed a
to them from the sky, causing their necks to bow before it in humility.

(As a result they would be forced to accept Imaan. However, Allaah does not do this because forcing people into submission would defeat the object of testing them to reward or punish them according to their merit.)
v.s: If We willed, We could send down to them from the sky a sign for which their necks would remain humbled.
v.c: If We willed, We could send down upon them a ˹compelling˺ sign from the heavens, leaving their necks bent in ˹utter˺ submission to it.

q: Whenever any new advice from Ar Rahmaan comes to them, they turn away from it
(refusing (to accept, so do not grieve over them).
v.s: And no mention [i.e., revelation] comes to them anew from the Most Merciful except that they turn away from it.
v.c: Whatever new reminder comes to them from the Most Compassionate, they always turn away from it.

q: (Besides turning away from Allaah's guidance and advice).
so shortly the news of what they used to mock will come to them.
(They will soon learn about the punishment that will afflict them because they mocked the advice that Allaah sent to them.)
v.s: For they have already denied, but there will come to them the news of that which they used to ridicule.
v.c: They have certainly denied ˹the truth˺, so they will soon face the consequences of their ridicule.

q: Have they not seen the earth and how We cause every impeccable species
v.s: Did they not look at the earth - how much We have produced therein from every noble kind?
v.c: Have they failed to look at the earth, ˹to see˺ how many types of fine plants We have caused to grow in it?

q: There is certainly a great Aayah in this
(which proves that Allaah is One and that He has tremendous powers).
most of them do not have Imaan.
v.s: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
v.c: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.

q: Verily your Rabb is Mighty, the Most Merciful.
v.s: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
v.c: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.

v.s: And [mention] when your Lord called Moses, [saying], "Go to the wrongdoing people -
v.c: ˹Remember˺ when your Lord called out to Moses, “Go to the wrongdoing people—

q: (and preach the message of Towheed to them).
v.s: The people of Pharaoh. Will they not fear God?"
v.c: the people of Pharaoh. Will they not fear ˹Allah˺?”

q: Moosa ﵊ said, “O my Rabb! I fear that they will reject me
(they will not believe that I am a Nabi).”
v.s: He said, "My Lord, indeed I fear that they will deny me
v.c: He replied, “My Lord! I fear that they will reject me.

q: my chest would tighten and that my tongue will not be able to move
v.s: And that my breast will tighten and my tongue will not be fluent, so send for Aaron.
v.c: And ˹so˺ my heart will be broken and my tongue will be tied. So send Aaron along ˹as a messenger˺.

q: and I fear that they will kill me
v.s: And they have upon me a [claim due to] sin, so I fear that they will kill me."
v.c: Also, they have a charge against me, so I fear they may kill me.”

q: (they will never be able to kill you)!
(to preach to Fir'oun and his people)
We are definitely listening to you two
(and will be there to assist you).'
v.s: [God] said, "No. Go both of you with Our signs; indeed, We are with you, listening.
v.c: Allah responded, “Certainly not! So go, both of you, with Our signs. We will be with you, listening.

q: “Go to Fir'oun and tell him, 'We are two messengers of the Rabb of the universe...”
v.s: Go to Pharaoh and say, 'We are the messengers of the Lord of the worlds,
v.c: Go to Pharaoh and say, ‘We are messengers from the Lord of all worlds,

q: (must release the Bani Israa'eel from captivity and)
send the Bani Israa'eel with us
v.s: [Commanded to say], "Send with us the Children of Israel."'"
v.c: ˹commanded to say:˺ ‘Let the Children of Israel go with us.’’”

q: “Did we not raise you among us as a newborn child? And did you not live with us for many years of your life
(How can you then act ungratefully; by telling me what to do)?”
v.s: [Pharaoh] said, "Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life?
v.c: Pharaoh protested, “Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you stayed several years of your life in our care?

q: that you did and you were ungrateful
(You benefited from my wealth and killed one of my men, and yet you want me to follow you).'
v.s: And [then] you did your deed which you did, and you were of the ungrateful."
v.c: Then you did what you did, being ˹utterly˺ ungrateful!”

q: at a time when I was from the mistaken ones
v.s: [Moses] said, "I did it, then, while I was of those astray [i.e., ignorant].
v.c: Moses replied, “I did it then, lacking guidance.

q: “I then fled from you people when I feared
(would not understand my case and kill me in retaliation).
My Rabb then granted me wisdom and included me among those sent
v.s: So I fled from you when I feared you. Then my Lord granted me judgement [i.e., wisdom and prophet hood] and appointed me [as one] of the messengers.
v.c: So I fled from you when I feared you. Then my Lord granted me wisdom and made me one of the messengers.

q: (that you raised me as a child)
(wish to overshadow the fact that you)
(However, the wrongs you do cannot be justified by the good you did).”
v.s: And is this a favor of which you remind me - that you have enslaved the Children of Israel?"
v.c: How can that be a ‘favour,’ of which you remind me, when ˹it was only because˺ you ˹have˺ enslaved the Children of Israel?”

q: Fir'oun said, “What is the Rabb of the universe
(Whose messenger do you claim to be)?”
v.s: Said Pharaoh, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?"
v.c: Pharaoh asked, “And what is ‘the Lord of all worlds’?”

q: The Rabb of the heavens, the earth and whatever is between the two; if you will be convinced
(if you wish to be convinced, understanding this is sufficient for you).”
v.s: [Moses] said, "The Lord of the heavens and earth and that between them, if you should be convinced."
v.c: Moses replied, “˹He is˺ the Lord of the heavens and the earth and everything in between, if only you had sure faith.”

q: to those around him, “Do you hear
v.s: [Pharaoh] said to those around him, "Do you not hear?"
v.c: Pharaoh said to those around him, “Did you hear ˹what he said˺?”

q: is your Rabb and the Rabb of your forefathers.”
v.s: [Moses] said, "Your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers."
v.c: Moses added, “˹He is˺ your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers.”

q: “Indeed your Rasool who has been sent to you is certainly insane.”
v.s: [Pharaoh] said, "Indeed, your 'messenger' who has been sent to you is mad."
v.c: Pharaoh said ˹mockingly˺, “Your messenger, who has been sent to you, must be insane.”

q: said, “He is the Rabb of the East, the West and whatever is between the two; if you are able to understand
(if you can understand this, you will be able to accept Imaan).”
v.s: [Moses] said, "Lord of the east and the west and that between them, if you were to reason."
v.c: Moses responded: “˹He is˺ the Lord of the east and west, and everything in between, if only you had any sense.”

q: said, “If you take another as an Ilaah besides myself, I shall definitely include you among the prisoners
(of my dungeons where you will suffer terribly)!”
v.s: [Pharaoh] said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely place you among those imprisoned."
v.c: Pharaoh threatened, “If you take any other god besides me, I will certainly have you imprisoned.”

q: (which proves that I am Allaah's messenger)?”
v.s: [Moses] said, "Even if I brought you something [i.e., proof] manifest?"
v.c: Moses responded, “Even if I bring you a clear proof?”

q: (in your claim that you are Allaah's messenger).”
v.s: [Pharaoh] said, "Then bring it, if you should be of the truthful."
v.c: Pharaoh demanded, “Bring it then, if what you say is true.”

q: threw down his staff and it suddenly became a manifest serpent.
v.s: So [Moses] threw his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent manifest.
v.c: So he threw down his staff and—behold!—it became a real snake.

v.s: And he drew out his hand; thereupon it was white for the observers.
v.c: Then he drew his hand ˹out of his collar˺ and it was ˹shining˺ white for all to see.

q: said to the ministers around him, “This is certainly a knowledgeable
v.s: [Pharaoh] said to the eminent ones around him, "Indeed, this is a learned magician.
v.c: Pharaoh said to the chiefs around him, “He is indeed a skilled magician,

q: to expel you from your land with his magic. What do you advise
v.s: He wants to drive you out of your land by his magic, so what do you advise?"
v.c: who seeks to drive you from your land by his magic. So what do you propose?”

q: replied, “Grant him and his brother respite
while you dispatch recruiters to the
v.s: They said, "Postpone [the matter of] him and his brother and send among the cities gatherers
v.c: They replied, “Let him and his brother wait and dispatch mobilizers to all cities

q: (so that they may challenge Moosa ﵊ to a contest of magic).”
v.s: Who will bring you every learned, skilled magician."
v.c: to bring you every skilled magician.”

q: gathered for an appointment on the specified day
(which was a day of festivity for the people).
v.s: So the magicians were assembled for the appointment of a well-known day.
v.c: So the magicians were assembled at the set time on the appointed day.

q: The people were asked, “Will you all gather
(at a particular place on the particular day)...'
v.s: And it was said to the people, "Will you congregate.
v.c: And the people were asked, “Will you join the gathering,

v.s: That we might follow the magicians if they are the predominant?"
v.c: so that we may follow the magicians if they prevail?”

q: they asked Fir'oun, “Shall we receive any prize
v.s: And when the magicians arrived, they said to Pharaoh, "Is there indeed for us a reward if we are the predominant?"
v.c: When the magicians came, they asked Pharaoh, “Shall we have a ˹suitable˺ reward if we prevail?”
v.h: Moses and the Magicians Face off

m: the ones who are brought near
q: said, “Certainly! Then you shall be from those who are close to me
v.s: He said, "Yes, and indeed, you will then be of those near [to me]."
v.c: He replied, “Yes, and you will then certainly be among those closest to me.”

v.s: Moses said to them, "Throw whatever you will throw."
v.c: Moses said to them, “Cast whatever you wish to cast.”

q: So they threw their ropes and staffs saying, “By Fir'oun's honour! We shall certainly be the victors
(because our ropes and staffs appear to be slithering snakes to the people)!”
v.s: So they threw their ropes and their staffs and said, "By the might of Pharaoh, indeed it is we who are predominant."
v.c: So they cast down their ropes and staffs, saying, “By Pharaoh’s might, it is we who will surely prevail.”

q: Then Moosa threw his staff, which
(the optical illusions made the people think that the snakes were real).
v.s: Then Moses threw his staff, and at once it devoured what they falsified.
v.c: Then Moses threw down his staff, and—behold!—it devoured the objects of their illusion!

q: (Realising that the feat of Moosa ﵊' was not mere magic, but something possible only with Allaah's help),
The magicians were cast down in prostration
(they were forced to prostrate before Allaah to show that they now believed in Allaah).
v.s: So the magicians fell down in prostration [to God].
v.c: So the magicians fell down, prostrating.

q: They submitted, “We believe in the Rabb of the universe...”
v.s: They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds,
v.c: They declared, “We ˹now˺ believe in the Lord of all worlds—

q: “...in the Rabb of Moosa ﵊ and Haaroon ﵊.”
v.s: The Lord of Moses and Aaron."
v.c: the Lord of Moses and Aaron.”

m: and I will surely crucify you
q: must certainly be your leader who has taught you magic! You shall shortly come to learn
(how I deal with people who refuse to worship me)!
I will cut off your hands and feet from opposite sides and crucify
v.s: [Pharaoh] said, "You believed him [i.e., Moses] before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic, but you are going to know. I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you all."
v.c: Pharaoh threatened, “How dare you believe in him before I give you permission? He must be your master who taught you magic, but soon you will see. I will certainly cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, then crucify you all.”

q: (what you do to us because we will still not reconsider our decision). (If you kill us)
We shall surely return to our Rabb
(Who will reward us for our Imaan).”
v.s: They said, "No harm. Indeed, to our Lord we will return.
v.c: They responded, “˹That would be˺ no harm! Surely to our Lord we will ˹all˺ return.

q: that our Rabb forgive our sins
because we have been the first Mu'mineen
v.s: Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins because we were the first of the believers."
v.c: We really hope that our Lord will forgive our sins, as we are the first to believe.”

q: (Finally, after Moosa ﵊ had preached to the people for many years)
We sent revelation to Moosa saying, “Lead My bondsmen
v.s: And We inspired to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued."
v.c: And We inspired Moses, ˹saying,˺ “Leave with My servants at night, for you will surely be pursued.”

q: (learnt that the Bani Israa'eel had left, he)
v.s: Then Pharaoh sent among the cities gatherers
v.c: Then Pharaoh sent mobilizers to all cities,

q: (Encouraging people to join the army, the recruiters announced),
v.s: [And said], "Indeed, those are but a small band,
v.c: ˹and said,˺ “These ˹outcasts˺ are just a handful of people,

v.s: And indeed, they are enraging us,
v.c: who have really enraged us,

q: (who are more than a match for them).”
v.s: And indeed, we are a cautious society..."
v.c: but we are all on the alert.”

v.s: So We removed them from gardens and springs
v.c: So We lured the tyrants out of ˹their˺ gardens, springs,

v.s: And treasures and honourable station -
v.c: treasures, and splendid residences.

m: And We caused to inherit them
q: This is how it was. And
(just as We had the power to remove them),
We made the Bani Israa'eel successors to them
(they lived on after the death of Fir'oun and his army).
v.s: Thus. And We caused to inherit it the Children of Israel.
v.c: So it was. And We awarded it ˹all˺ to the Children of Israel.

v.s: So they pursued them at sunrise.
v.c: And so they pursued them at sunrise.

q: set eyes on each other, Moosa ﵊ people said, “We will surely be caught
(because they are behind us and the sea is in front of us).”
v.s: And when the two companies saw one another, the companions of Moses said, "Indeed, we are to be overtaken!"
v.c: When the two groups came face to face, the companions of Moses cried out, “We are overtaken for sure.”

q: “Never!” replied Moosa, “My Rabb is with me and He will certainly guide me
v.s: [Moses] said, "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me."
v.c: Moses reassured ˹them˺, “Absolutely not! My Lord is certainly with me—He will guide me.”

q: So We sent revelation to Moosa telling him, “Strike the sea with your staff.”
(creating twelve paths for them to cross to the other side),
(each wall of water between the paths)
v.s: Then We inspired to Moses, "Strike with your staff the sea," and it parted, and each portion was like a great towering mountain.
v.c: So We inspired Moses: “Strike the sea with your staff,” and the sea was split, each part was like a huge mountain.

q: (to the sea, making them enter after the Bani Israa'eel).
v.s: And We advanced thereto the others [i.e., the pursuers].
v.c: We drew the pursuers to that place,

q: So We rescued Moosa ﵊ and all those who were with him
(allowing them to cross safely to the other side).
v.s: And We saved Moses and those with him, all together.
v.c: and delivered Moses and those with him all together.

q: (Fir'oun's army when the paths in the sea closed up before they could reach the shore).
v.s: Then We drowned the others.
v.c: Then We drowned the others.

q: There is certainly a great Aayah in this
(incident for people of all times, which teaches people that failure to accept Imaan leads to destruction).
most of them do not have Imaan.
v.s: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
v.c: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.

q: (ready to forgive anyone who repents sincerely).
v.s: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
v.c: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.

v.s: And recite to them the news of Abraham,
v.c: Relate to them ˹O Prophet˺ the story of Abraham,

q: When he said to his people and to his father, “What do you worship?”
v.s: When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"
v.c: when he questioned his father and his people, “What is that you worship ˹besides Allah˺?”

q: They replied, “We worship idols and we are devoted to them.”
v.s: They said, "We worship idols and remain to them devoted."
v.c: They replied, “We worship idols, to which we are fully devoted.”

q: He asked, “Do they hear you when you call to them?”
v.s: He said, "Do they hear you when you supplicate?
v.c: Abraham asked, “Can they hear you when you call upon them?

q: “Or can they benefit or harm you?”
(How can you worship such helpless things?)
v.s: Or do they benefit you, or do they harm?"
v.c: Or can they benefit or harm you?”

q: we found our forefathers doing the same.”
v.s: They said, "But we found our fathers doing thus."
v.c: They replied, “No! But we found our forefathers doing the same.”

v.s: He said, "Then do you see what you have been worshipping,
v.c: Abraham responded, “Have you ˹really˺ considered what you have been worshipping—

q: (Have you not considered your position carefully)?”
v.s: You and your ancient forefathers?
v.c: you and your ancestors?

q: (whose worship causes harm instead of good),
except the Rabb of the universe
(Allaah, Whose worship brings only good and no harm).'
v.s: Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds,
v.c: They are ˹all˺ enemies to me, except the Lord of all worlds.

q: Who has created me and Who guides me
v.s: Who created me, and He [it is who] guides me.
v.c: ˹He is˺ the One Who created me, and He ˹alone˺ guides me.

q: “Who feeds me and gives me drink...”
v.s: And it is He who feeds me and gives me drink.
v.c: ˹He is˺ the One Who provides me with food and drink.

q: “...and Who cures me when I am ill
v.s: And when I am ill, it is He who cures me
v.c: And He ˹alone˺ heals me when I am sick.

q: Who will grant me death and then give me life again
v.s: And who will cause me to die and then bring me to life
v.c: And He ˹is the One Who˺ will cause me to die, and then bring me back to life.

q: Who I hope will forgive my shortcomings on the Day of Qiyaamah.”
v.s: And who I aspire that He will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense."
v.c: And He is ˹the One˺ Who, I hope, will forgive my flaws on Judgment Day.”

q: “O my Rabb! Grant me wisdom and join me with the righteous
v.s: [And he said], "My Lord, grant me authority and join me with the righteous.
v.c: “My Lord! Grant me wisdom, and join me with the righteous.

q: “Maintain a favourable word for me among those who are to come
(let all the people who are to come after me speak only good of me).'
v.s: And grant me a mention [i.e., reputation] of honour among later generations.
v.c: Bless me with honourable mention among later generations.

q: “And make me from the inheritors of the bounteous Jannah
v.s: And place me among the inheritors of the Garden of Pleasure.
v.c: Make me one of those awarded the Garden of Bliss.

q: “Forgive my father, for he is among those who have gone astray.”
(Ibraheem ﵊ made this du'aa with the hope that Allaah will guide his father to accept Imaan. Once a person has died as a Kaafir, it is not permissible to make du'aa asking forgiveness for him/her.)
v.s: And forgive my father. Indeed, he has been of those astray.
v.c: Forgive my father, for he is certainly one of the misguided.

q: “Do not disgrace me on the Day
v.s: And do not disgrace me on the Day they are [all] resurrected -
v.c: And do not disgrace me on the Day all will be resurrected—

q: “...the day when neither wealth nor sons will be of any benefit
(will be unable to save anyone from punishment)...”
v.s: The Day when there will not benefit [anyone] wealth or children
v.c: the Day when neither wealth nor children will be of any benefit.

q: (that these will be a source of benefit)
for him who comes to Allaah with a sound
(a heart free of Shirk).” (The wealth and children of such a person can benefit him because he would have used these in Allaah's obedience, thereby earning reward for this in the Aakhirah).
v.s: But only one who comes to God with a sound heart."
v.c: Only those who come before Allah with a pure heart ˹will be saved˺.”

q: Jannah will be brought close to the pious
v.s: And Paradise will be brought near [that Day] to the righteous.
v.c: ˹On that Day˺ Paradise will be brought near to the God-fearing,

q: ...while Jahannam will be revealed to the deviant ones
v.s: And Hellfire will be brought forth for the deviators,
v.c: and the Hellfire will be displayed to the deviant.

v.s: And it will be said to them, "Where are those you used to worship
v.c: And it will be said to them, “Where are those you used to worship

q: Can they assist you or protect you
v.s: Other than God? Can they help you or help themselves?"
v.c: besides Allah? Can they help you or even help themselves?”

q: will all be thrown headlong into it
v.s: So they will be overturned into it [i.e., Hellfire], they and the deviators
v.c: Then the idols will be hurled headlong into Hell, along with the deviant

v.s: And the soldiers of Iblees, all together.
v.c: and the soldiers of Iblîs, all together.

v.s: They will say while they dispute therein,
v.c: There the deviant will cry while disputing with their idols,

q: ...“By Allaah! We were certainly in manifest
v.s: "By God, we were indeed in manifest error
v.c: “By Allah! We were clearly mistaken,

q: “...when we considered you to be equal to the Rabb of the universe
v.s: When we equated you with the Lord of the worlds.
v.c: when we made you equal to the Lord of all worlds.

v.s: And no one misguided us except the criminals.
v.c: And none led us astray other than the wicked.

q: “Now there is no intercessor for us...”
v.s: So now we have no intercessors
v.c: Now we have none to intercede for us,

v.s: And not a devoted friend.
v.c: nor a close friend.

q: “If only we were given the chance to return
Then we would be among the Mu'mineen.”
v.s: Then if we only had a return [to the world] and could be of the believers..."
v.c: If only we could have a second chance, then we would be believers.”

q: There is certainly a great Aayah
most of them do not have Imaan.
v.s: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
v.c: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.

q: Verily your Rabb is Mighty, the Most Merciful.
v.s: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
v.c: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.

q: The people of Nooh ﵊ rejected those sent to them
(Although the people during his time rejected his message, they are said to have rejected all the Ambiyaa ﵊ because all the Ambiyaa ﵊ carried the same message).
v.s: The people of Noah denied the messengers
v.c: The people of Noah rejected the messengers

q: When their brother Nooh ﵊ said to them, “Do you not fear
(even a little of Allaah's punishment for committing Shirk)?”
v.s: When their brother Noah said to them, "Will you not fear God?
v.c: when their brother Noah said to them, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?

v.s: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
v.c: I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.

v.s: So fear God and obey me.
v.c: So fear Allah, and obey me.

q: “I do not ask you for any payment for this
Allaah, the Rabb of the universe.”
v.s: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
v.c: I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.

v.s: So fear God and obey me."
v.c: So fear Allah, and obey me.”

q: They replied, “Should we believe in you when
the lowest of people follow you blindly without question?”
(How can we follow you when those who are poor and who do menial jobs follow you? How can we mix with them? Are they perhaps not after wealth and status?)
v.s: They said, "Should we believe you while you are followed by the lowest [class of people]?"
v.c: They argued, “How can we believe in you, when you are followed ˹only˺ by the lowest of the low?”

q: said, “Why should I be concerned about their deeds
(their occupation?” What difference does their occupations make to their Imaan”)
v.s: He said, "And what is my knowledge of what they used to do?
v.c: He responded, “And what knowledge do I have of what they do?

q: “(If they are insincere, I cannot verify this because)
(I cannot turn them away as long as they profess Imaan.)
(understand this, you would not look down on them)!”
v.s: Their account is only upon my Lord, if you [could] perceive.
v.c: Their judgment is with my Lord, if you had any sense!

q: “I shall never drive away the Mu'mineen
(just so that you may sit with me).”
v.s: And I am not one to drive away the believers.
v.c: I am not going to expel the believers.

q: (warning you of a grave punishment if you continue to make absurd demands and refuse to accept imaan).”
v.s: I am only a clear warner."
v.c: I am only sent with a clear warning.”

q: They said, “O Nooh! If you do not desist
you will certainly be of those who are stoned
v.s: They said, "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be of those who are stoned."
v.c: They threatened, “If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be stoned ˹to death˺.”

q: (Finally, after preaching to them for 950 years)
said, “O my Rabb! My people have rejected me
v.s: He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.
v.c: Noah prayed, “My Lord! My people have truly rejected me.

q: and rescue me and those Mu'mineen who are with me.”
v.s: Then judge between me and them with decisive judgement and save me and those with me of the believers."
v.c: So judge between me and them decisively, and save me and the believers with me.”

q: and those with him in a laden ark
(which contained all the Mu'mineen as well as a pair of every living species).
v.s: So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.
v.c: So We saved him and those with him in the fully loaded Ark.

v.s: Then We drowned thereafter the remaining ones.
v.c: Then afterwards We drowned the rest.

q: There is certainly a great Aayah
in this. However, most of them do not have Imaan.
v.s: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
v.c: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.

q: Verily your Rabb is Mighty, the Most Merciful.
v.s: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
v.c: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.

v.s: ʿAad denied the messengers
v.c: The people of ’Âd rejected the messengers

q: When their brother Hood ﵊ said to them, “Do you not fear
(a little of Allaah's punishment for committing Shirk)?”
v.s: When their brother Hūd said to them, "Will you not fear God?
v.c: when their brother Hûd said to them, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?

v.s: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
v.c: I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.

v.s: So fear God and obey me.
v.c: So fear Allah, and obey me.

q: ''I do not ask you for any payment for this
Allaah, the Rabb of the universe.”
v.s: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
v.c: I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.

v.s: Do you construct on every elevation a sign, amusing yourselves,
v.c: ˹Why˺ do you build a landmark on every high place in vanity,

q: “And do you construct large palaces so that, perchance, you may live forever
(thinking that you will never have to leave them and that death cannot reach you in them)?”
v.s: And take for yourselves constructions [i.e., places and fortresses] that you might abide eternally?
v.c: and construct castles, as if you are going to live forever,

q: (oppressing them and showing no mercy to) them)?”
v.s: And when you strike, you strike as tyrants.
v.c: and act so viciously when you attack ˹others˺?

v.s: So fear God and obey me.
v.c: So fear Allah, and obey me.

q: (is much more Powerful than you and Who)
you with the things that you know
(with the knowledge you have and everything that you possess)...”
v.s: And fear He who provided you with that which you know,
v.c: Fear the One Who has provided you with ˹the good˺ things you know:

v.s: Provided you with grazing livestock and children
v.c: He provided you with cattle, and children,

q: (all of which contribute to your prosperity and dominance).'
v.s: And gardens and springs.
v.c: and gardens, and springs.

q: I fear for you the punishment
v.s: Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible day."
v.c: I truly fear for you the torment of a tremendous day.”

q: They replied, “It is immaterial to us whether you advise us or whether you are not from the advisors
(regardless of what you do, we will not accept your advice).”
v.s: They said, "It is all the same to us whether you advise or are not of the advisors.
v.c: They responded, “It is all the same to us whether you warn ˹us˺ or not.

q: is merely the behaviour of the old men
v.s: This is not but the custom of the former peoples,
v.c: This is simply the tradition of our predecessors.

q: (in any way. Your warnings are therefore in vain).'
v.s: And we are not to be punished."
v.c: And we will never be punished.”

q: They rejected him so We destroyed them
There is certainly a great Aayah
in this. However, most of them do not have Imaan.
v.s: And they denied him, so We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
v.c: So they rejected him, and ˹so˺ We destroyed them. Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.

q: (Powerful enough to destroy whoever He wills),
(Most Forgiving to pardon whoever repents sincerely).
v.s: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
v.c: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful. Prophet Ṣâliḥ

v.s: Thamūd denied the messengers
v.c: The people of Thamûd rejected the messengers

q: When their brother Saalih ﵊ said to them, “Do you not fear
(even a little of Allaah's punishment for committing Shirk)?”
v.s: When their brother Sālih said to them, “Will you not fear God?
v.c: when their brother Ṣâliḥ said to them, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?

v.s: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
v.c: I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.

v.s: So fear God and obey me.
v.c: So fear Allah, and obey me.

q: “I do not ask you for any payment for this
Allaah, the Rabb of the universe.”
v.s: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
v.c: I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.

q: be left in peace with what is here
(in this world without having to leave it all behind after death and without having to answer for everything you say and do)?”
v.s: Will you be left in what is here, secure [from death],
v.c: Do you think you will be ˹forever˺ left secure in what you have here:

q: “(Do you think that you will be left in peace)
v.s: Within gardens and springs
v.c: amid gardens and springs,

q: “...plantations and date palms with heavily laden stalks
(your date palms that bear dates in abundance)?”
v.s: And fields of crops and palm trees with softened fruit?
v.c: and ˹various˺ crops, and palm trees ˹loaded˺ with tender fruit;

q: (in addition to thinking that you will remain in the world forever)
you boastfully carve homes from the mountains
(thinking that they will save you from death).”
v.s: And you carve out of the mountains, homes, with skill.
v.c: to carve homes in the mountains with great skill?

v.s: So fear God and obey me.
v.c: So fear Allah, and obey me.

v.s: And do not obey the order of the transgressors,
v.c: And do not follow the command of the transgressors,

q: and who do not make amends
v.s: Who cause corruption in the land and do not amend."
v.c: who spread corruption throughout the land, never setting things right.” Ṣâliḥ’s People Destroyed

q: said, “You are merely one of the
v.s: They said, "You are only of those affected by magic.
v.c: They replied, “You are simply bewitched!

q: “You are merely a human like us
(to prove that you really are a Rasool)
if you are from the truthful
(if you are true in your claim to Prophethood).”
v.s: You are but a man like ourselves, so bring a sign, if you should be of the truthful."
v.c: You are only a human being like us, so bring forth a sign if what you say is true.”

q: (When the Thamud then requested Saalih ﵊ to extract a pregnant camel from a mountain, he made du'aa to Allaah, Who granted the request. When the camel emerged from the mountain),
(that you asked for). (Because of its great size),
and your animals will have an appointed day exclusively for them to drink.”
v.s: He said, "This is a she-camel. For her is a [time of] drink, and for you is a [time of] drink, [each] on a known day.
v.c: Ṣâliḥ said, “Here is a camel. She will have her turn to drink as you have yours, each on an appointed day.

q: of a dreadful day will afflict you.”
v.s: And do not touch her with harm, lest you be seized by the punishment of a terrible day."
v.c: And do not ever touch her with harm, or you will be overtaken by the torment of a tremendous day.”

v.s: But they hamstrung her and so became regretful.
v.c: But they killed her, becoming regretful.

q: There is certainly a great Aayah
in this. However, most of them do not have Imaan.
v.s: And the punishment seized them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
v.c: So the punishment overtook them. Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.

q: (Powerful enough to destroy whoever He wills),
(Most Forgiving to pardon whoever repents sincerely).
v.s: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
v.c: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.

q: The nation of Loot ﵊ rejected those sent
v.s: The people of Lot denied the messengers
v.c: The people of Lot rejected the messengers

q: When their brother Loot ﵊ said to them, “Do you not fear
v.s: When their brother Lot said to them, "Will you not fear God?
v.c: when their brother Lot said to them, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?

v.s: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
v.c: I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.

v.s: So fear God and obey me.
v.c: So fear Allah, and obey me.

q: “I do not ask you for any payment for this
Allaah, the Rabb of the universe.”
v.s: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
v.c: I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.

v.s: Do you approach males among the worlds
v.c: Why do you ˹men˺ lust after fellow men,

q: “...leaving aside your wives whom your Rabb has created for you
You are certainly a transgressing nation
(who have transgressed the limits of morality and of pure human nature to do such a vile act).”
v.s: And leave what your Lord has created for you as mates? But you are a people transgressing."
v.c: leaving the wives that your Lord has created for you? In fact, you are a transgressing people.”

q: They replied, “O Loot! If you do not desist
you will surely be from those who are banished
v.s: They said, "If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be of those evicted."
v.c: They threatened, “If you do not desist, O Lot, you will surely be expelled.”

q: “(There is no way in which I shall ever desist from trying to stop you people because)
I am certainly among those who detest your action.”
v.s: He said, "Indeed, I am, toward your deed, of those who detest [it].
v.c: Lot responded, “I am truly one of those who despise your ˹shameful˺ practice.

q: (However, when the people refused to listen to him despite his tireless efforts to change them, he finally made du'aa to Allaah saying),
“O my Rabb! Save me and my family from what
(and from the punishment that is due to them because of their evil ways).”
v.s: My Lord, save me and my family from [the consequence of] what they do."
v.c: My Lord! Save me and my family from ˹the consequences of˺ what they do.”

q: (when Our punishment came to his community,)
and all the members of his family...
v.s: So We saved him and his family, all,
v.c: So We saved him and all of his family,

q: who was among those who were left behind
(to die in the punishment because she was a Kaafir as well).
v.s: Except an old woman among those who remained behind.
v.c: except an old woman, who was one of the doomed.

q: (after saving Loot ﵊ and the other Mu'mineen)
v.s: Then We destroyed the others.
v.c: Then We utterly destroyed the rest,

q: upon them. Evil indeed was the rain on those who were forewarned.
(Although they had been warned about Allaah's punishment, they refused to mend their ways and were finally destroyed.)
v.s: And We rained upon them a rain [of stones], and evil was the rain of those who were warned.
v.c: pouring upon them a rain ˹of brimstone˺. How evil was the rain of those who had been warned!

q: There is certainly a great Aayah in this. However, most of them do not have Imaan
v.s: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
v.c: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.

q: (Powerful enough to destroy whoever He wills),
(Most Forgiving to pardon whoever repents sincerely).
v.s: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
v.c: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.

v.s: The companions of the thicket [i.e., the people of Madyan] denied the messengers
v.c: The residents of the Forest rejected the messengers

q: When their brother Shu'ayb ﵊ said to them, “Do you not fear
v.s: When Shuʿayb said to them, "Will you not fear God?
v.c: when Shu’aib said to them, “Will you not fear ˹Allah˺?

q: “I am certainly a trustworthy messenger to you.”
v.s: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
v.c: I am truly a trustworthy messenger to you.

v.s: So fear God and obey me.
v.c: So fear Allah, and obey me.

q: “I do not ask you for any payment for this
Allaah, the Rabb of the universe.”
v.s: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
v.c: I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺. My reward is only from the Lord of all worlds.

q: in full and do not be of those who reduce
(the amount of the goods being sold while accepting full payment for it).'
v.s: Give full measure and do not be of those who cause loss.
v.c: Give full measure, and cause no loss ˹to others˺.

q: (without cheating your customers in any way).”
v.s: And weigh with an even [i.e., honest] balance.
v.c: Weigh with an even balance,

q: (by giving them less than what they were paid for)
and do not spread corruption on earth
(by robbing people and devouring their rights).”
v.s: And do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on earth, spreading corruption.
v.c: and do not defraud people of their property. Nor go about spreading corruption in the land.

q: “Fear the Being Who created you and all the previous creations.”
v.s: And fear He who created you and the former creation."
v.c: And fear the One Who created you and ˹all˺ earlier peoples.”

q: They said, “You must surely be one of the
v.s: They said, "You are only of those affected by magic.
v.c: They replied, “You are simply bewitched!

q: “You are merely a human like ourselves
(you are no better than us, so why should we obey you?).
(less than a human like us because you are)
v.s: You are but a man like ourselves, and indeed, we think you are among the liars.
v.c: Also, you are only a human being like us, and we think you are indeed a liar.

q: “So cause a piece of the sky to fall on us
if you are from the truthful ones
(if you are really a Rasool and if your warnings of punishment are true and not mere idle threats).'
v.s: So cause to fall upon us fragments of the sky, if you should be of the truthful."
v.c: So cause ˹deadly˺ pieces of the sky to fall upon us, if what you say is true.”

q: said, “My Rabb knows best what you do
(He knows everything you do and therefore knows what punishment you deserve and exactly when the punishment should arrive.)
v.s: He said, "My Lord is most knowing of what you do."
v.c: Shu’aib responded, “My Lord knows best whatever you do.”

q: rejected him and the punishment of the day of the canopy seized them. It was certainly a punishment of a dreadful day.

(When Allaah made the weather extremely hot, all the people left their homes and sought shelter beneath the trees. Allaah then sent a dense cloud towards them, which they mistook as a “canopy” to escape from the heat. When they gathered beneath the cloud, a descending fire scorched them all.)
v.s: And they denied him, so the punishment of the day of the black cloud seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a terrible day.
v.c: So they rejected him, and ˹so˺ were overtaken by the torment of the day of the ˹deadly˺ cloud. That was really a torment of a tremendous day.

q: There is certainly a great Aayah
in this. However, most of them do not have Imaan
(even after listening to these truthful events).
v.s: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
v.c: Surely in this is a sign. Yet most of them would not believe.

q: (Powerful enough to destroy whoever He wills),
(Most Forgiving to pardon whoever repents sincerely).
v.s: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
v.c: And your Lord is certainly the Almighty, Most Merciful.

q: is a revelation from the Rabb of the universe.
v.s: And indeed, it [i.e., the Qur’ān] is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds.
v.c: This is certainly a revelation from the Lord of all worlds,

q: The trustworthy angel descended with it
v.s: The Trustworthy Spirit [i.e., Gabriel] has brought it down
v.c: which the trustworthy spirit ˹Gabriel˺ brought down

q: so that you become of those
(people about the grave consequences of rejecting Imaan)...
v.s: Upon your heart, [O Muhammad] - that you may be of the warners -
v.c: into your heart ˹O Prophet˺—so that you may be one of the warners—

v.s: In a clear Arabic language.
v.c: in a clear Arabic tongue.

q: (they therefore knew about its revelation to Rasulullaah ﷺ a long time ago).
v.s: And indeed, it is [mentioned] in the scriptures of former peoples.
v.c: And it has indeed been ˹foretold˺ in the Scriptures of those before.

q: Is it not sufficient proof for them
that the scholars of the Bani Israa'eel know about it?

(The fact that the scholars of the Bani Israa'eel knew about the coming of the Qur'aan and of Rasulullaah ﷺ before Rasulullaah ﷺ was born is ample proof that this was mentioned in their scriptures. Many of their learned scholars who accepted Islaam attested to this, as did many of them who did not accept Islaam).
v.s: And has it not been a sign to them that it is recognized by the scholars of the Children of Israel?
v.c: Was it not sufficient proof for the deniers that it has been recognized by the knowledgeable among the Children of Israel?

q: If We were to reveal it
v.s: And even if We had revealed it to one among the foreigners
v.c: Had We revealed it to a non-Arab,

q: ...who was to recite it to them
they would have still not believed in it.

(The miracle of the Qur'aan would have seemed more profound if a non-Arab had brought it to the Mushrikeen of Makkah because then there would have been no way in which they could have said that he had written it by himself. However, the Mushrikeen of Makkah were so stubborn that even then they would have rejected the Qur'aan).
v.s: And he had recited it to them [perfectly], they would [still] not have been believers in it.
v.c: who would then recite it to the deniers ˹in fluent Arabic˺, still they would not have believed in it!

q: (just as kufr was set deep in the hearts of the Mushrikeen of Makkah)
in the hearts of the sinners.
v.s: Thus have We inserted it [i.e., disbelief] into the hearts of the criminals.
v.c: This is how We allow denial ˹to steep˺ into the hearts of the wicked.

v.s: They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment.
v.c: They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment,

m: And it will come to them
q: when they do not perceive it
(without giving them a chance to accept imaan).
v.s: And it will come to them suddenly while they perceive [it] not.
v.c: which will take them by surprise when they least expect ˹it˺.

q: (to change our ways and accept Imaan)?” (This will be impossible.)
v.s: And they will say, "May we be reprieved?"
v.c: Then they will cry, “Can we be allowed more time?”

m: So is it for Our punishment
q: Do they seek to hasten Our punishment
(by constantly asking when it will arrive)?
v.s: So for Our punishment are they impatient?
v.c: Do they ˹really˺ seek to hasten Our torment?

q: Tell me. If We were to allow them
v.s: Then have you considered if We gave them enjoyment for years
v.c: Imagine ˹O Prophet˺ if We allowed them enjoyment for years,

q: should come to them which they were promised...
v.s: And then there came to them that which they were promised?
v.c: then there came to them what they had been threatened with:

q: (The enjoyment will be useless to them. If anything, it may only warrant greater punishment for them if they had misused extra time granted for them).
v.s: They would not be availed by the enjoyment with which they were provided.
v.c: would that enjoyment be of any benefit to them ˹at all˺?

q: We have destroyed towns only after they had
v.s: And We did not destroy any city except that it had warners
v.c: We have never destroyed a society without warners

q: (them about the terrible consequences of rejecting Imaan). (Therefore),
(because We never punished anyone without first warning him about the consequences of his behaviour).
v.s: As a reminder; and never have We been unjust.
v.c: to remind ˹them˺, for We would never wrong ˹anyone˺.

q: The Shayaateen have not brought it
v.s: And the devils have not brought it [i.e., the revelation] down.
v.c: It was not the devils who brought this ˹Quran˺ down:

q: (because while the Qur'aan provides guidance, the Shayaateen can provide only misguidance),

(to overhear any part of the Qur'aan in the heavens before it was transmitted to Rasulullaah ﷺ because Allaah had sealed off the corridors to the heavens for them and whoever tried to overhear something was destroyed by a flaming star).
v.s: It is not allowable for them, nor would they be able.
v.c: it is not for them ˹to do so˺, nor can they,

q: have definitely been forbidden from listening
(to the revelation of the Qur'aan in the heavens).
v.s: Indeed they, from [its] hearing, are removed.
v.c: for they are strictly barred from ˹even˺ overhearing ˹it˺.

q: Do not call to another Ilaah besides Allaah, for then you will be of the punished ones.
v.s: So do not invoke with God another deity and [thus] be among the punished.
v.c: So do not ever call upon any other god besides Allah, or you will be one of the punished.

q: (about the punishment that is due to those who reject Imaan). (When this verse was revealed, Rasulullaah ﷺ gathered his entire tribe together and warned them about the punishment for rejecting Imaan).
v.s: And warn, [O Muhammad], your closest kindred.
v.c: And warn ˹all, starting with˺ your closest relatives,

q: to those Mu'mineen who follow you.
v.s: And lower your wing [i.e., show kindness] to those who follow you of the believers.
v.c: and be gracious to the believers who follow you.

q: disobey you, then say, “Verily I am innocent of that
v.s: And if they disobey you, then say, "Indeed, I am disassociated from what you are doing."
v.c: But if they disobey you, say, “I am certainly free of what you do.”

q: on the Mighty, the Most Merciful...
v.s: And rely upon the Exalted in Might, the Merciful,
v.c: Put your trust in the Almighty, Most Merciful,

v.s: Who sees you when you arise
v.c: Who sees you when you rise ˹for prayer at night˺,

q: ...and sees your movements with those who prostrate
v.s: And your movement among those who prostrate.
v.c: as well as your movements ˹in prayer˺ along with ˹fellow˺ worshippers.

q: Without doubt, He is the All Hearing, the All Knowing
(and will reward you for all the good you do).
v.s: Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
v.c: He ˹alone˺ is indeed the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

q: Should I inform you about the one on whom the Shayaateen descend
v.s: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?
v.c: Shall I inform you of whom the devils ˹actually˺ descend upon?

v.s: They descend upon every sinful liar.
v.c: They descend upon every sinful liar,

q: (from the discussions of the angels about future events)
and most of them are liars
(together with something they overhear from the angels, they tell the fortune-tellers hundreds of lies).
v.s: They pass on what is heard, and most of them are liars.
v.c: who gives an ˹attentive˺ ear ˹to half-truths˺, mostly passing on sheer lies.

q: Only deviant people follow the poets
(by repeating those poems of theirs that contain rambling speech and useless talk).
v.s: And the poets - [only] the deviators follow them;
v.c: As for poets, they are followed ˹merely˺ by deviants.

q: Do you not see that they
(have no direction and tend to sway to the extremes)?
v.s: Do you not see that in every valley they roam
v.c: Do you not see how they rant in every field,

q: that they say things which they never do?
v.s: And that they say what they do not do? -
v.c: only saying what they never do?

q: (Such is the condition of all poets)
Except those who have Imaan, who do good acts, who remember Allaah abundantly and who avenge themselves after being oppressed
(by counteracting the satirical poetry that the Kuffaar direct at Islaam with true poetry of their own). (Although they refuse to believe in the Aakhirah),
will come to know to which place they will return
v.s: Except those [poets] who believe and do righteous deeds and remember God often and defend [the Muslims] after they were wronged. And those who have wronged are going to know to what [kind of] return they will be returned.
v.c: Except those who believe, do good, remember Allah often, and ˹poetically˺ avenge ˹the believers˺ after being wrongfully slandered. The wrongdoers will come to know what ˹evil˺ end they will meet.
